condition: localized mild 3 cm itchy red poison ivy rash streak on right ankle after hike
level_rationale: Having a localized mild 3 cm red streak of itchy rash on the right ankle 2 days after brushing against poison ivy while hiking in a 29-year-old adult is minor plant-induced skin irritation suitable for over-the-counter soothing calamine or hydrocortisone lotion self-care, whereas developing large fluid blisters wrapping 15 cm around that same ankle after poison ivy contact indicates severe extensive bullous plant reaction warranting an outpatient doctor visit for prescription corticosteroid therapy rather than self-care lotion or emergency care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain self-care dermatologic register swap ('a pruritic eruption on my right ankle in a mild 3 cm erythematous streak' vs 'an itchy rash on my right ankle in a mild 3 cm red streak') + single-fact same-ankle bullous extent escalation control (-cf, mild 3 cm red streak to large fluid blisters wrapping 15 cm around that ankle, L1 to L2).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic facts (age 29, brushed against poison ivy while hiking 2 days ago, itchy rash on the right ankle, and mild 3 cm red streak) without naming dermatitis and with zero 'without...' stated negatives. Escalating rash severity and extent strictly at the already-named right ankle ('in a mild 3 cm red streak' to 'with large fluid blisters wrapping 15 cm around it') adds zero unstated body locations (SPEC.md section 5.5) while shifting care from OTC soothing lotion (level 1) to outpatient physician prescription steroid evaluation (level 2) under Rules A, B, and D.
